headline: Analysis pipeline choices flip or create reported effects in brain-model and network comparisons
label: Evaluation Protocol Sensitivity
summary: Three preprints show analysis choices alter conclusions in model-brain RSA and EEG rich-club work, and one audits a brain-response model against sensory maps.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that analysis-pipeline decisions, not only the model or network under study, can determine reported conclusions. A multiverse reanalysis of THINGS fMRI RSA shows that choices such as centring change whether untrained or trained CNNs better model V1. In Alzheimer's disease EEG, rich-club results depend on null network construction and hub re-identification, which can create or erase group differences. The TRIBE v2 audit differs in aim: it tests a multimodal fMRI response model against classic sensory maps, reporting no retinotopy or tonotopy but strong MT+ motion selectivity. It shares the scrutiny theme only loosely. What is new is treating analysis choices as explicit experimental variables. All three are preprints, so findings remain preliminary.
